approach.method_basis: The Parent moves persistent particles through a fixed molecular autoencoder. Each particle retains its current position and velocity, remembers its best actually scored generating position, and is pulled toward that personal best and the best resolved position found by the swarm. A frozen deterministic decoder turns each proposed position into a molecule. Accepted scores update memories only at the exact position that produced their molecular identity. Initially, the encoder supplies particle locations, but an initial molecule can supply a scored attractor only when decoding its encoding reproduces that molecule. In the observed run this worked for just one of the ten supplied molecules.
approach.novelty: Add bounded latent inversion at initialization: move only the input coordinates of each initially mismatched molecule to make its known token sequence preferred by the frozen decoder. Install a refined position only after an exact canonical reconstruction check succeeds, so additional known scores can become usable swarm attractors. Failed refinements retain the original initialization. This is the first Child in the lineage; the Parent tried direct encoder placement but never corrected its coordinates through the decoder. The experiment tests recovery of scored starting positions before proposing any change to the subsequent swarm motion.

hypothesis: At objective initialization, refine each identity-mismatched initial encoding by bounded gradient descent on frozen-decoder target-token margin loss, and replace its particle starting position and admit its real initial score only when unchanged deterministic decoding exactly recovers that initial canonical molecule.

finding_summary.headline: One initial molecule became a working swarm attractor, but the macro score fell from 0.451 to 0.348
finding_summary.insights: At least one missing starting identity was already representable by the frozen decoder: correcting its coordinates recovered that identity without changing neural weights or transferring a score to a different molecule. The causal path from recovery to installation, motion and scored attraction is therefore established. That repairs a real coverage defect, but this run does not support the expectation that doubling the initially scored particles improves overall search quality. On drd2_docking and sitagliptin, both recovered personal memories were replaced after their first proposals, before they could supply a nonzero personal pull; their shared memory still influenced other particles. On deco_hop, the recovered shared attractor was referenced in 210 motions and both recovered personal memories survived to the end, yet the task score was lower. The amount of attractor reuse alone is therefore insufficient evidence of useful search guidance. All nine optimization attempts lowered their best visited mean loss, but only one recovered its molecule, so the token-margin proxy cannot replace the production identity check. The eight failures do not establish that those molecules lack an inverse: the bounded local optimizer may simply have failed to find one. Mean decoded fingerprint distance from the source remained large, increasing from 0.854 to 0.864. The molecular assessment likewise finds abundant rings alongside long unsaturated chains, labile polar linkers and irregular ring arrangements. Exact initialization does not control those downstream structural changes. Broader inversion coverage and the usefulness of moves around a recovered position remain separate open questions; this single seed establishes activation and an observed score loss, without establishing a reproducible score effect.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aryl and amine outputs still rely on polyenes, labile polar linkers and enlarged heterocycles
molecular.overall_character: The supplied seed-0 trajectories cover all five tasks, each with 300 observed molecules including 290 optimizer proposals. The offspring are mostly medium-sized organic structures with aryl groups, nitrogen/oxygen functionality, nonaromatic unsaturated rings and frequent alkene/imine extensions. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9655 to 0.9966, while aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.4621 to 0.8724. These are fractions of proposal strings containing the respective feature, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. There is substantial variation in connectivity, but recurring polyene, imine and expanded-ring chemistry limits its medicinal-chemistry breadth. Conventional amides, ethers, biaryls and cyclic amines are present; chemically questionable linker and ring contexts often accompany them. All five stereocentre-marker rates are 0.0, although some cited connectivities have unspecified stereogenic centres. The parent comparison shows different chemical families at the score extremes, without establishing which individual structural change caused a score change. The principal missing capability is reliable production of coherent, stable functional-group and ring arrangements; simple ring closure is already abundant.

per_task.generated_character: Relatively compact aryl-containing molecules, with mean SMILES length 38.5; ring-closure and aromatic-token rates are 0.9931 and 0.8724. Phenyl, fluorophenyl, pyridyl and furyl groups occur beside unsaturated nitrogen rings, imines, hydrazone/imidic-acid motifs, ethers and occasional conventional amides. Halogen presence is 0.5138. The highest molecule combines phenyl and fluorophenyl surfaces with an expanded unsaturated nitrogen-containing ring. The elementary functional groups are familiar, but many complete structures would require careful route, tautomer and stability assessment.
liabilities: Terminal methylene imines and extended imine/enamine or vinyl-ether sequences introduce stability and geometric-isomer concerns.

The hydroxy-imine motifs require tautomer assessment; their notation alone does not establish that they are impossible molecules. Large bridged or expanded unsaturated rings also complicate synthesis and conformational control.
missing_features: The low end lacks the compact combination of aryl surface and suitably placed nitrogen/oxygen functionality illustrated by the high end; adding more rings or longer linkers does not supply that balance.

Conventional compact polar scaffolds like the supplied indole carboxamide are not consistently represented among the offspring; many analogous polar features instead sit in imine networks or expanded rings.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 206 scores 0.39044078347364974 and evaluation 104 scores 0.3779644730092272: both combine aryl groups with nitrogen/oxygen functionality in fairly compact structures. The bulky alkyl-linked polycyclic amide at evaluation 27 scores 8.222310670560957e-27 despite carrying rings, aromatics and polar groups. Thus the visible association is with their overall size and arrangement, not the mere presence of those features. The initial indole carboxamide already scores 0.3051048083696145 with more conventional connectivity. Relative to the parent high end, brominated carbonyl/nitrile structures have given way to imine/imidic-acid aryl structures; the observed best changes from 0.37483330611175764 to 0.39044078347364974. per_task.generated_character: Larger polyunsaturated structures, averaging 53.3 SMILES characters, with ring-closure rate 0.9931 but aromatic-token rate only 0.4621. The upper end includes nitrile-substituted phenyl groups, aryl amines, amides/lactams, methoxy/ethoxy groups and occasional acids. These fragments are often joined through extended conjugated chains or enlarged heterocycles; the highest molecule contains a nitrile-bearing aniline substituent on a large fused unsaturated lactam system. Such topologies are synthetically less straightforward than the recognizable fragments suggest.
liabilities: Long conjugated chains, vinyl ethers and expanded rings create geometric-isomer and conformational questions that the SMILES do not resolve.
Evaluation 238 contains unusual C=[SH] bonding alongside a large imine-rich ring, warranting explicit valence-state and stability assessment before treating it as ordinary synthetic chemistry.
missing_features: Lower-scoring outputs do not retain the linked aryl and polar donor/acceptor contexts recurring in the stronger examples; nonaromatic ring closure alone supplies little discrimination.

Its related aza-ring analogue at 295 gives 0.07627084463732096, so adding nitrogen does not by itself reproduce the best polar arrangement. The observed separation is mainly compatible with a size/composition and polar-group-arrangement preference; aromaticity is not a sufficient explanation. The digest median is displayed as 0.0 despite the positive reported minimum. Compared with the parent, aromatic-token presence rises from 0.2621 to 0.7241 and ring closure from 0.6759 to 0.9655, but the observed best changes from 0.259395205519374 to 0.18042079374720374. transferable_gaps.evidence: The proposal ring-closure rates are 0.9655 to 0.9966, yet the digest repeatedly shows enlarged unsaturated nitrogen rings, complex bridged systems and long polyenes attached to otherwise familiar aryl groups. The aryl hydrazone/imidic-acid hit at 0.39044078347364974 and the nitrile-bearing lactam at 0.5531131032788899 both illustrate expanded ring contexts. The biaryl pyrrolidinone at 0.17680640316934415 demonstrates that conventional small saturated ring chemistry is within the observed output.
transferable_gaps.gap: Abundant ring closure is not accompanied by reliable control of ordinary ring topology and molecular size.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide more routine access to coherent aromatic and saturated ring frameworks and chemically controlled changes in ring connectivity and substituent size. Preserve useful aryl and polar fragments while varying their arrangement without automatically extending conjugated chains or enlarging rings. Assess unusual macrocycles and bridged systems individually; their ring-closure syntax alone is neither a quality guarantee nor proof of impossibility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Terminal imines, imidic-acid/hydrazone forms, enamine-linked aldehydes and vinyl ethers recur in the cited high and low examples. The upper end at 0.4125494085104425 retains an amine/aryl combination but also an aldehyde and conjugated enamine linker. A chloramine-containing enal scores 0.0006956176616831638, and a late proposal contains phosphorus-chloride bonding. Conventional aryl amides, cyclic ureas and a pyrrolidinone elsewhere in the digest provide chemically recognizable alternative contexts.
transferable_gaps.gap: Polar functionality is too often expressed through labile conjugated linkers or unusual reactive bonding contexts.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand coverage of stable amine, amide/urea and ether environments with controlled spacing and substitution, so polar diversity does not require repeated alkene/imine sequences. Treat tautomer/protonation representation separately from genuinely reactive bonds, and apply the same structure-based chemical plausibility criteria to every generated molecule. The observed scores do not establish that replacing a liability will automatically improve an objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest task reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. Nevertheless, the cited biaryl pyrrolidinone, substituted epoxide and several bridged cyclic amines contain stereogenic centres without an assigned configuration. The trajectories also show conjugated and substituted alkene sequences without specified geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereogenic connectivity unspecified throughout the observed output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically consistent stereochemical specification when constructing stereogenic centres or configurable double bonds, including preservation of configurations across related structures. This is an observed gap in molecular specification; no supplied comparison establishes a score preference for a particular stereoisomer.

method_name: Molecule Swarm Optimization with persistent latent velocities
method_thesis: Anchor the method in Molecule Swarm Optimization: each particle keeps its latent position, velocity and best observed position, and moves through inertia plus independent stochastic attractions toward its personal best and the swarm's best. [Winter et al., Methods 2.2-2.4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6836962/) describe this molecular use of particle swarm optimization. For our adaptation, train a compact SELFIES VAE solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus, freeze its encoder and deterministic decoder, and start each objective with clean swarm memories. Encodings of supplied molecules provide starting geometry; their scores initialize attractors only when decoding preserves canonical molecular identity. Otherwise establish scored attractors from actual generated evaluations, never from mislabeled reconstructions. Generate fresh latent positions through particle motion and decode new complete molecules. Locally retry stochastic motion for invalid or duplicate outcomes until the announced batch is filled. Match accepted feedback to the exact generating position before updating personal and shared bests; each batch uses only resolved memories. The corpus supplies a generator, never a molecule library for ranking or retrieval. The hypothesis is that persistent individual trajectories explore alternatives while shared successful locations redirect them quickly enough to improve the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. This uses the provided scalar objective directly, without additional desirability terms. Useful latent geometry and rapid transfer of discoveries between particles remain empirical prerequisites. The published model and evaluation scale do not establish those prerequisites under the permitted preparation and scarce feedback.

research_intent.falsifier: The proposed initial-anchor recovery does not activate on the supplied conditions if no originally mismatched initial identity is recovered and installed, even if input optimization decreases its token-margin loss. An absent/nonfinite gradient on every eligible nonstationary target, optimizing anything other than the latent inputs, failing to follow the registered bounded update, or never using a recovered position as a particle motion source also defeats the intended causal path. Missing receipts make the corresponding claim inconclusive. The scored-memory transfer subclaim remains unestablished when recovered memories have no eligible later attraction opportunity, and is refuted if such opportunities exist but the registered memories are never referenced. Unreachable targets and worse decoded geometry after otherwise valid recovered initialization remain possible failure causes.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich aryl and amine outputs still rely on polyenes, labile polar linkers and enlarged heterocycles
molecular_assessment.overall_character: The supplied seed-0 trajectories cover all five tasks, each with 300 observed molecules including 290 optimizer proposals. The offspring are mostly medium-sized organic structures with aryl groups, nitrogen/oxygen functionality, nonaromatic unsaturated rings and frequent alkene/imine extensions. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9655 to 0.9966, while aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.4621 to 0.8724. These are fractions of proposal strings containing the respective feature, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. There is substantial variation in connectivity, but recurring polyene, imine and expanded-ring chemistry limits its medicinal-chemistry breadth. Conventional amides, ethers, biaryls and cyclic amines are present; chemically questionable linker and ring contexts often accompany them. All five stereocentre-marker rates are 0.0, although some cited connectivities have unspecified stereogenic centres. The parent comparison shows different chemical families at the score extremes, without establishing which individual structural change caused a score change. The principal missing capability is reliable production of coherent, stable functional-group and ring arrangements; simple ring closure is already abundant.

per_task.generated_character: Relatively compact aryl-containing molecules, with mean SMILES length 38.5; ring-closure and aromatic-token rates are 0.9931 and 0.8724. Phenyl, fluorophenyl, pyridyl and furyl groups occur beside unsaturated nitrogen rings, imines, hydrazone/imidic-acid motifs, ethers and occasional conventional amides. Halogen presence is 0.5138. The highest molecule combines phenyl and fluorophenyl surfaces with an expanded unsaturated nitrogen-containing ring. The elementary functional groups are familiar, but many complete structures would require careful route, tautomer and stability assessment.
liabilities: Terminal methylene imines and extended imine/enamine or vinyl-ether sequences introduce stability and geometric-isomer concerns.

The hydroxy-imine motifs require tautomer assessment; their notation alone does not establish that they are impossible molecules. Large bridged or expanded unsaturated rings also complicate synthesis and conformational control.
missing_features: The low end lacks the compact combination of aryl surface and suitably placed nitrogen/oxygen functionality illustrated by the high end; adding more rings or longer linkers does not supply that balance.

Conventional compact polar scaffolds like the supplied indole carboxamide are not consistently represented among the offspring; many analogous polar features instead sit in imine networks or expanded rings.
